11.text: The same may be said regarding the ceremonials. The individual cere-

12.text: monials — those connected with death, burial, and marriage — are much the

13.text: same among the two branches of the Chukchee and the Asiatic Eskimo.

14.text: The family ceremonials are arranged in a regular cycle, are celebrated

15.text: from season to season throughout the year, and are directly connected with

16.text: the pursuits of material life; therefore those of the reindeer-breeders differ

17.text: from those of the maritime people. In this respect the difference between

18.text: the Reindeer Chukchee and the Asiatic Eskimo is still greater. Some of the

19.text: ceremonials of the Maritime Chukchee bear a resemblance to those of the

20.text: Reindeer people, and show only such changes as result from their diversity

21.text: in material culture. Many of their ceremonials are similar to the religious

22.text: rites of the Asiatic Eskimo. In this respect, as in many others, the customs

23.text: of the Maritime Chukchee occupy a middle ground between those of the

24.text: Asiatic Eskimo and those of the Reindeer Chukchee. Each family, moreover,

25.text: has its peculiar groups of images and ceremonials, characterized by special

26.text: details, and differing from those used by neighboring families. These dif-

27.text: ferences develop continually under orders received from shamans, or directly

28.text: from spirits through dreams. In this way, even the chief ceremonials of the

29.text: year come to be observed somewhat differently by neighboring camps and

30.text: by different families in the same villages.

31.text: AMULETS. — The charms of both the Reindeer and the Maritime Chuk-

32.text: chee are used as amulets; that is, as objects having peculiar power, which

33.text: they may use for the benefit of a person who has possession of them.
